rows.speaker: السخاوي
rows.claim: A report in al-Sakhawi’s al-Maqasid al-hasana says the speaker saw al-Khidr through his mother’s filial piety.
rows.anchor: قال : ببرك أمك كما في "المقاصد الحسنة" للإمام السخاوي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should show unqualified kindness to both parents; filial devotion guides to Paradise and brings safety in hardship.
rows.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يكون بارا بوالديه مطلقا أنفسين أو أفاقيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book means the Qur’an, or this noble sura as part of the Book; Mary’s story is meant because remembrance attaches to her account, not her person.
rows.anchor: القرآن أو السورة الكريمة فإنها بعض من الكتاب فصح إطلاقه عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maryam means worshipper.
rows.anchor: ومريم بمعنى العابدة

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: God names Mary openly to affirm her motherhood and servitude, refute Christian claims about her and Jesus, and make repeated maternal attribution disavow a father and clear her from Jewish slander.
rows.anchor: صرح الله تعالى باسمها ولم يكن عنها تأكيدا للأموة والعبودية التي هي صفة لها

rows.speaker: أسئلة الحكم
rows.claim: Mary is named because she devoted herself to obedience like a complete man and was addressed in the manner of prophets.
rows.anchor: وقال في "أسئلة الحكم" : سميت مريم في القرآن باسمها لأنها أقامت نفسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some held that Mary had prophethood.
rows.anchor: ولذا قيل : بنبوتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time phrase attaches to the omitted word story; nabdh means casting away, and intibadh is its derived form.
rows.anchor: ظرف لذلك المضاف من النبذ وهو الطرح والانتباذ افتعال منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary withdrew from her people to an eastern place, construed as the destination of implied going.
rows.anchor: من قومها متعلق بانتبذت

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Christians face east and Jews west because the appointed meeting and Torah’s giving occurred on the mountain’s western side.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن ومن ثمة اتخذ النصارى المشرق قبلة كما اتخذ اليهود المغرب قبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary secluded herself at her aunt Eshaa’s house near the sun; she stayed in the mosque when pure and went to her aunt’s house during menstruation, then came to wash in winter.
rows.anchor: فإذا حاضت تحولت إلى بيت خالتها وإذا طهرت عادت إلى المسجد

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: The screen was a curtain that prevented people from seeing her.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (رده كه مانع باشد ازديدن)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel appeared as a handsome, bright-faced, curly-haired, beardless young man; he is called spirit because of his subtle spiritual nature and because religion comes alive through him.
rows.anchor: أتاها الملك في صورة آدمي شاب أمرد وضيىء الوجه جعد الشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel is called spirit because he is spiritual and subtle and religion is enlivened through him.
rows.anchor: جبريل فإنه كان روحانيا فأطلق عليه الروح للطافته مثله ولأن الدين يحيى به

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: Gabriel is literally spirit in his abstract reality and figuratively so in his imaginal form; abstract spirits can assume forms and convey life, explaining the life in the Samiri’s calf from Gabriel’s trace.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الكبار جبرائيل هو الروح حقيقة باعتبار حقيقته المجردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation calls Gabriel spirit figuratively as an affectionate term, like telling a beloved person you are my spirit.
rows.anchor: وقيل سماه روحا مجازا محبة له وتقريبا كقولك أنت روحي لمن تحب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His complete human form made Mary comfortable enough to hear God’s words and suited his task of breathing life that would produce a human child.
rows.anchor: لتستأنس بكلامه وتتلقى منه ما يلقي إليها من كلماته تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage alludes to conception after complete purification, making the child more excellent.
rows.anchor: القربان بعد الطهر التام أطهر والولد إذن أنجب

rows.speaker: التأويلات
rows.claim: Spirit is the light of God’s creative Word, called spirit because it revives dead hearts; the light and spirit terms can be exchanged, and tawhid’s light appears in the confession of faith.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات" : الروح هو نور كلمة الله التي يعبر عنها بقوله كن

rows.speaker: التأويلات
rows.claim: Jesus is from the light of the Word cast to Mary; when that Word took human form, she did not recognize it and sought refuge in God.
rows.anchor: نور من لقائه فلما تمثلت الكلمة بالبشر أنكرتها مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary invokes the Merciful by that name to intensify her appeal and draw the special mercy that protects her.
rows.anchor: ذكره تعالى بعنوان الرحمانية للمبالغة في العياذ به تعالى

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Her taking refuge in God from a beautiful young man demonstrates her chastity and scrupulousness.
rows.anchor: دل على عفافها وورعها أنها تعوذت بالله من تلك الصورة الجميلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional answer is omitted because context makes it clear: she is taking refuge in God.
rows.anchor: جواب الشرك محذوف ثقة بدلالة السياق عليه أي : فإني عائذة به

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: A God-fearing person takes warning from God, whereas a sinner is deterred by rulers and a hypocrite by people.
rows.anchor: التقي يتعظ بالله ويخاف والفاسق يخوف بالسلطان والمنافق يخوف بالناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel clarifies that he is the Lord’s messenger, not a man from whom she should expect the evil she feared.
rows.anchor: لست ممن يتوقع منه ما توهمت من الشر وإنما أنا رسول ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel would be the means of the boy’s gift by breathing into the garment; zakiy means pure of sins and the darkness of the human ego.
rows.anchor: لأكون سببا في هبته بالنفخ في الدرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary’s question expresses ordinary astonishment, not doubt about divine power.
rows.anchor: استبعادا ظاهرا أي : متعجبة من حيث العادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Touch is a euphemism for lawful intercourse; calling him a human intensifies her denial of physical approach, while bighy means a woman who seeks illicit sex.
rows.anchor: فإن المس كناية عن الوطىء الحلال أما الزنى فإنما يقال خبث بها أو فجر

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: Bighy is not feminine in form because this description commonly applies to women like the word menstruating; it means a fornicator who seeks men.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل بغية لأنه وصف غالب على المؤنث كحائض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary excludes both possible causes of a child: lawful intercourse is denied because no man touched her, and illicit intercourse because she was not a prostitute.
rows.anchor: يريد نفي الوطىء مطلقا وأن الولد إما من النكاح الحلال أو الحرام

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Her added denial of future intercourse reflects that she is consecrated and marriage is forbidden to her.
rows.anchor: ليمسسني بشر بعد هذا بالزنى أو بالنكاح لأني محررة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer confirms what Mary said: no one touched her, yet creating the child without any human cause is easy for God.
rows.anchor: ما ذكرت من هبة الغلام من غير أن يمسك بشر أصلا

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: God creates Jesus from the light of the Word kun, as He created Adam from earth and then said be.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {قال كذالك} الذي تقولين ولكن {قال ربك هو على هين}

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Jesus is a sign that God can create without a father, just as Adam was created without father or mother and Eve without a mother.
rows.anchor: قادر على أن أخلق ولدا من غير أب كما أني خلقت آدم من غير أب وأم

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Jesus is a great mercy whose guidance leads people; being made a mercy means being imbued with God’s attribute, unlike merely admitting someone into mercy and Paradise.
rows.anchor: ومن جعله رحمة منه يجعله متصفا بصفته وكذا بين قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The child’s creation was decreed in primordial knowledge and cannot fail; knowing the secret of destiny makes hardships easier.
rows.anchor: قضيت به في سابق علمي وحكمت بوقوعه لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All events unfold under ancient wisdom according to differing capacities; one who receives good should thank God, and one who receives otherwise should blame only himself.
rows.anchor: العلم تابع للمعلوم فكل ما يقتضيه من الأحوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trials burn away blameworthy dispositions, while patience produces divine and true qualities.
rows.anchor: بالبلاء تحترق الأوصاف الرديئة الخلقية وبالصبر يحصل الأخلاق الإلهية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Mary accepted Gabriel’s words; he came near, blew into her garment’s opening, and the breath reached her womb, so she conceived immediately.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما فاطمأنت مريم إلى قول جبريل فدنا منها فنفخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Breath can reach the body without an opening; Adam’s spirit entered through the crown of his head and then spread through the body.
rows.anchor: وصول النفخ إلى الجوف لا يحتاج إلى منفذ من المنافذ كالفم ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus has bodily, spiritual, and unifying aspects: his body suggests Mary’s fluid, his reviving miracles suggest Gabriel’s breath, and their synthesis points to both.
rows.anchor: لعيسى عليه السلام جهة جسمانية وجهة روحانية وأحدية جمع للجهتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi says Gabriel’s human appearance caused Mary’s pleasure and fluid to enter the womb, so Jesus formed from her fluid; this rejects naturalists’ denial that one parent’s fluid alone can produce a child.
rows.anchor: فهو من ماء أمه فقط خلافا للطبيعيين فإنهم ينكرون وجود الولد من ماء أحد الزوجين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The full human body came through Mary’s fluid and Gabriel’s human likeness preserved the usual human pattern; her imagining fluid made it occur, and the spirit’s endurance explains Jesus’ prolonged human form.
rows.anchor: وقد توهمت في النفخ الماء فحصل الماء المتوهم أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without Gabriel’s human likeness, Jesus would have appeared as a spirit; if Gabriel breathed while Mary was fearful, the child would inherit her harsh state.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : لو لم يتمثل جبريل عند النفخ بالصورة البشرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stories say a mother’s sight at conception can shape a child, including snake-like and bear-like offspring, illustrating the transmission of parental states.
rows.anchor: نقل في الأخبار : أن امرأة ولدت ولدا صورته صورة البشر وجسمه جسم الحية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary relaxed after hearing Gabriel was sent by God and recalled the angels’ good news; conception in that open-hearted state made Jesus open-hearted too.
rows.anchor: فنفخ فيها في حين الانبساط والانشراح فخرج عيسى منبسطا منشرح الصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says Mary was thirteen and had menstruated twice before conception, and recommends that strong people imagine a well-formed man during intercourse.
rows.anchor: قالوا : حملته وسنها وقتئذ ثلاث عشرة سنة وقد حاضت حيضتين قبل أن تحمل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas gives the pregnancy and birth duration as one hour; some considered this strongest because Jesus was created directly, and the sequential fāʾ supports immediacy.
rows.anchor: ففي رواية عن ابن عباس كانت مدة الحمل والولادة ساعة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ marks accompaniment or state: she withdrew while carrying Jesus in her womb; the distant place is construed as a destination reached by going.
rows.anchor: فاعتزلت ملتبسة به أي : وهو في بطنها

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Mary went from Jerusalem to a distant mountain or valley near Bethlehem, about six miles from Iliya.
rows.anchor: مكاني دورز شهر ايليا كويند بكوهى رفت درجانب شرقي

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet’s Isra account that Gabriel said he prayed at Bethlehem, where Jesus was born; Bursevi calls the report authentic or hasan and cites al-Nasa’i and al-Bayhaqi.
rows.anchor: وعن أنس رضي الله عنه أنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في حديث الإسراء

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: An alternative location is the far side of the house, which better fits the short pregnancy duration.
rows.anchor: أو أقصى الدار وهو الأنسب لقصر مدة الحمل

rows.speaker: قصص الأنبياء
rows.claim: As birth approached, Mary left Zakariya’s house at night for a place outside Jerusalem, wishing that Zakariya and others would not know.
rows.anchor: لما دنت ولادة مريم خرجت في حوف الليل من منزل زكريا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aja’a is the causative of jā’a, meaning labor brought and compelled Mary; makhad is the pain of childbirth and the child’s movement toward delivery.
rows.anchor: تعدية جاء بالهمزة أي : جاء بها واضطرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She went to the palm trunk for privacy and support because no midwife was present; the story says she sat by a dry palm at night.
rows.anchor: لتستتر به وتعتمد عليه عند الولادة إذ لم تكن لها قابلة تعينها

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The labor brought her to the trunk to display a miracle there.
rows.anchor: في "التأويلات النجمية" : {فأجآءها المخاض إلى جذع النخلة} لإظهار المعجزة في الجذع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trunk was the lower palm stem; it was dry, without crown or greenery, and miraculously bore winter fruit to calm Mary and feed a postpartum mother.
rows.anchor: وكانت نخلة يابسة لا رأس لها ولا خضرة وكان الوقت شتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading of mittu with kasra follows māta-yamātu; another reading with damma follows māta-yamūtu.
rows.anchor: وهو بكسر الميم من مات يمات كخفت وقرىء بضمها من مات يموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary wished to have died from shame and fear of people’s blame or provoking sinful accusations, not from rejecting God’s promise; righteous people also voiced such wishes under severe distress.
rows.anchor: استحياء من الناس على حكم العادة البشرية لا كراهة لحكم الله

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: In severe distress Umar wished he had been merely a straw and nothing at all.
rows.anchor: عن عمر رضي الله عنه أنه أخذ تبنة من الأرض فقال : يا ليتني هذه التبنة

rows.speaker: بلال
rows.claim: Bilal likewise wished his mother had never given birth to him.
rows.anchor: عن بلال أنه قال : ليت بلالا لم تلده أمه

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Her wish is interpreted as wishing to die before pregnancy, since some would accuse her of adultery and others call her son God’s son, leading many to Hell.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {قبل هاذا} أي : قبل هذا الحمل فإنه بسبب حملي وولدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasyan is an insignificant thing normally forgotten, while mansiy intensifies the sense of being absent from everyone’s mind.
rows.anchor: شيئا حقيرا شأنه أن ينسى ولا يعتد به أصلا

rows.speaker: التأويلات
rows.claim: Nasyan mansiy is interpreted as being in nonexistence, unremembered by God through not being brought into being.
rows.anchor: في "التأويلات" : {نسيا منسيا} في العدم لا يذكرني الله بالإيجاد

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi explains Mary’s anguish as shame at being known by Jerusalem’s people as an unmarried virgin in Zakariya’s care who now gives birth.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : (يعني هيكس مرا اندانستى وازمن حساب نداشتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The voice came from below Mary, from a place lower than her beneath the hill; another account places it beneath the palm.
rows.anchor: من مكان أسفل منها تحت الأكمة

rows.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
rows.claim: On a reading with fatḥah on the mīm, the one beneath her is Jesus, calling to her after emerging from the womb.
rows.anchor: وفي "الأسئلة المقحمة" قرىء بفتح الميم يعني به عيسى لما خرج من البطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command not to grieve concerns Jesus’ birth and the dry place; grief is sorrow over lost benefit or present harm, and the particle is explanatory or a verbal noun with a suppressed preposition.
rows.anchor: أن مفسرة بمعنى أي : لا تحزني بولادة عيسى وبمكان القحط

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Gabriel struck the earth and a fresh-water spring flowed as a brook; sariyy is a small stream as the Prophet explained.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن جبريل ضرب برجله الأرض فظهرت عين ماء عذب

rows.speaker: أرباب الحقيقة
rows.claim: Jesus announced prophethood in the cradle and, while still in the womb, sariyy signaled that he would be a lord and leader among people.
rows.anchor: سيدا على القوم بالنبوة انتهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hazz is forceful repeated motion in opposing directions; ilayki specifies direction, the bāʾ reinforces the verb, and Arabic allows both shaking it and shaking by it.
rows.anchor: هز الشيء تحريكه إلى الجهات المتقابلة تحريكا عنيفا متداركا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasāqat describes repeated falling of ripe dates, which are plucked before drying and ready to harvest.
rows.anchor: تساقط} أي : تسقط النخلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary should eat the dates and drink from the stream; the event was a preliminary sign for Jesus or a gracious gift to Mary, not a miracle because no challenge was made.
rows.anchor: وكان ذلك إرهاصا لعيسى أو كرامة لأمه وليس بمعجزة لفقد شرطها وهو التحدي

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: Food is mentioned before water because Mary needed it more after losing much blood.
rows.anchor: قدم الأكل لأن حاجتها إليه أشد من حاجتها إلى الماء لكثرة ما سال منها من الدماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although fear can hurt more than hunger or thirst, the fear was slight because Gabriel had reassured her, so God did not need to address it again.
rows.anchor: كان الخوف قليلا لبشارة جبريل فلم يحتج إلى التذكير مرة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dates are customary postpartum food; newborns are also given a date rubbed on the palate, and a hadith recommends fresh dates for a new mother, or dates if unavailable.
rows.anchor: إذا ولدت امرأة فليكن أول ما تأكل الرطب فإن لم يكن رطب فتمر

rows.speaker: الربيع بن خيثم
rows.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Khuthaym says dates are the best food for a postpartum woman and honey for a sick person.
rows.anchor: قال الربيع بن خيثم : ما للنفساء عندي خير من الرطب ولا للمريض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarr ayna means be at ease and let go of sorrow; the river, green palm, and out-of-season fruit vindicate Mary by showing God’s power to create a child without a man.
rows.anchor: فإن الله تعالى قد نزه ساحتك بالخوارق من جري النهر واخضرار النخلة اليابسة

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: The lexicon explains qarrat ayn as an eye cooling, its weeping stopping, or its seeing what it longed for.
rows.anchor: قرت عينه تقر بالكسر والفتح قرة ويضم وقرورا بردت وانقطع بكاؤها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another derivation connects the phrase to coolness: tears of joy are cold and tears of grief are hot, hence expressions of coolness and heat of the eye for loved and hated things.
rows.anchor: دمعة السرور باردة ودمعة الحزن حارة

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi says Mary could rejoice either in her son or in the tree’s greening and fruit, both signs that God can produce dates from a dry tree and a child without a father.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : (وقري عينا وروشن ساز شم را يفرزند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says every newborn cries except Jesus.
rows.anchor: قالوا : ما من مولود يستهل غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In fa-immā the mīm is extra, the construction strengthens the conditional, and the emphatic nūn accompanies the verb.
rows.anchor: وما مزيدة لتأكيد معنى الشرط وهي بمنزلة لام القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary’s vow obligates her; sawm means silence or fasting, and Israelite ascetics abstained from food and speech until evening, a practice later prohibited for Muslims.
rows.anchor: صمتا أو صياما وكان صيام المجتهدين من بني إسرائيل بالإمساك عن الطعام

rows.speaker: أبكار الأذكار
rows.claim: Silence in its proper time is a quality of spiritual masters, just as speech in its proper place is an excellent trait.
rows.anchor: قال في أبكار الأذكار السكوت في وقته صفة الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ascetics prefer silence because speech serves the ego through self-display and praise; ignorant pre-Islamic silence was forbidden and Muslims were directed to good speech and remembrance.
rows.anchor: لعلمهم بما في الكلام من حظ النفس وإظهار صفات المدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibited practice is absolute silence; abstaining from people’s speech while maintaining remembrance is accepted and even required, and sustained silence is one of eight conditions of the spiritual path.
rows.anchor: وأما السكوت عن كلام الناس مع ملازمة الذكر فمقبول بل مأمور به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary was to convey her vow by gesture rather than speech, so her silence means speaking to God and angels instead of human beings.
rows.anchor: أمرت بأن تخبر بنذرها بالإشارة فالمعنى قولي ذلك بالإشارة لا باللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary came back to her people with Jesus after recovering from childbirth; the bāʾ may mean accompanied by him or mark the transitive verb.
rows.anchor: جاءتهم مع ولدها راجعة إليهم عندما طهرت من نفاسها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Mary left at sunrise and returned at noon carrying the infant.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنها خرجت من عندهم حين شرقت الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story says Zakariya sent Yusuf to look for Mary, found her under the palm, and the righteous household wept when she returned.
rows.anchor: روي أن زكريا افتقد مريم فلم يجدها في محرابها فاغتم غما شديدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fary describes an immense, bizarre, or fabricated deed; it derives from cutting leather and al-Akhtari says it can mean either good or bad.
rows.anchor: عظيما بديعا منكرا مقطوعا بكذبه من فرى الجلد

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi glosses the accusation as something unprecedented among a household of good people.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (يزى شكفت يا زشت كه در ميان اهل بيت

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet’s report says Aaron meant the prophet Aaron; Mary belonged to the descendants or brotherly line associated with him, though he lived eighteen centuries earlier.
rows.anchor: روي عن النبي عليه السلام أنهم إنما عنوا به هارون النبي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says Aaron was Mary’s righteous brother by the same father.
rows.anchor: وكان بينها وبينه ألف وثمانمائة سنة وقيل كان هارون أخاها من أبيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies him as Moses’ brother and calls Mary his sister through descent, as one may say brother of the Arabs.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو أخو موسى نسبت إليه بالأخوة لأنها من ولده

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the question about Mary’s father as saying that Imran was not an adulterer.
rows.anchor: ما كان عمران زانيا قاله ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary’s father was Imran and her mother was Hanna daughter of Faqūdh; bighy means an adulteress, so the people infer that the child has no husband as its father.
rows.anchor: حنة بنت فاقوذ {بغيا} زانية فمن أين لك هذا الولد من غير زوج

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi describes Imran as a good man and one of the most distinguished scholars of the Jerusalem mosque.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (نبوددرتو عمران مردى بد بلكه مردى كه مسجد اقصارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When children of righteous people commit indecency, it is more heinous; most people reject prophets and saints as mad or false, while a few believe those returning with extraordinary knowledge.
rows.anchor: ارتكاب الفواحش من أولاد الصالحين أفحش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary pointed to Jesus so they would question him and his answer would serve as proof for her; she apparently indicated her vow and refusal to converse with people.
rows.anchor: إلى عيسى أن كلموه ليجيبكم ويكون كلامه حجة لي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people reject her gesture because they had never known an infant in a cradle to understand speech and answer rationally.
rows.anchor: ولم نعهد فيما سلف صبيا رضيعا في الحجر يكلمه عاقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāna may place the event in past time near or far, but here the nearby time follows from their astonishment; it can also be extra or complete in construction.
rows.anchor: وكان لإيقاع مضمون الجملة في زمان ماض مبهم صالح لقريبه وبعيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi prefers the view that kāna verifies the child’s infancy as an accomplished fact.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن كان لتحقيق صباوته فإن الماضي دال على التحقق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus answers in a clear voice and begins by professing servitude to God, refuting Christians’ claim to his divinity and clearing God and his mother of immorality.
rows.anchor: أقر على نفسه بالعبودية أول ما تكلم ردا على من يزعم بربوبيته

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Al-Junayd says he is neither a base slave, nor a slave of greed, nor of desire; servitude is the best human designation.
rows.anchor: قال الجنيد لست بعبد سوء ولا عبد طمع ولا عبد شهوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi’s sheikh ranks Abd Allah above Abd al-Rahman, then Abd al-Rahim and Abd al-Karim; divine essence names outrank attribute names, which outrank names of acts.
rows.anchor: عبد الله فوق عبد الرحمن وهو فوق عبد الرحيم وهو فوق عبد الكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says Zakariya was the person who questioned Jesus.
rows.anchor: المستنطق لعيسى زكريا وقد أكرم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Four children received special gifts: Joseph revelation in the well, Jesus speech in the cradle, Solomon understanding, and John wisdom in childhood.
rows.anchor: أكرم الله تعالى أربعة من الصبيان بأربعة أشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad received greater distinctions from infancy, including prostration at birth, opening of the breast, prophetic seal, angelic service, and prophethood in the spirit world before birth.
rows.anchor: وأكرم بالنبوة في عالم الأرواح قبل الولادة والصباوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book is the Gospel; Jesus was made beneficial and a teacher of good wherever he went, and the past tense states what was certain to happen.
rows.anchor: نفاعا معلما للخير أخبر عما يكون لا محالة بصيغة الماضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most commentators say God gave Jesus the Gospel and prophethood in childhood, when he had adult understanding; Bursevi notes the view that revelation came after thirty and messengership followed prophethood.
rows.anchor: الجمهور على أن عيسى آتاه الله الإنجيل والنبوة في الطفولية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus is blessed wherever he is; God emphatically commanded prayer and prescribed financial zakat for him.
rows.anchor: أمرني بها أمرا مؤكدا {والزكواة} أي : زكاة المال ملكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The zakat command does not prove Jesus was wealthy: it may apply to wealthy followers and is addressed to prophets to urge their communities.
rows.anchor: إيصاءه بها لا يستلزم غناء بل هي بالنسبة إلى أغنياء أمته

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Outward obligations do not lapse while a servant lives; claiming otherwise, as some permissive antinomians do, is disbelief and error.
rows.anchor: فيه دلالة بينة على أن العبد ما دام حيا لا يسقط عنه التكاليف

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The verse inwardly signals that a living servant must keep watch over the heart, uphold servitude, and purify the ego.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : فيه إشارة إلى أنه ما دام العبد حيا لا بد من مراقبة السر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obligations serve purification for beginners and gratitude for the advanced; neither ceases during adulthood, though insanity and similar conditions excuse a person.
rows.anchor: إقامة التكاليف عبودية وهي إما للتزكية كالمبتدئين وإما للشكر كالمنتهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus was made kind and gentle to his mother, an allusion to having no father; jabbār means arrogant and oppressive, and shaqī means disobedient to God.
rows.anchor: جعلني بارا بها محسنا لطيفا وهو إشارة إلى أنه بلا فحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Peace protects Jesus from Satan’s touch at birth, the hardships of death, and the terror of resurrection and Hell; the same protection came to John.
rows.anchor: بلا والد طبيعي أي : من طعن الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite peace may mean peace in full, while asserting peace for himself implicitly curses his enemies; the phrase in 20:47 likewise implies punishment for deniers.
rows.anchor: فإن إثبات جنس السلام لنفسه تعريض لإثبات ضده لأضداده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Jesus spoke, people knew Mary was chaste and innocent; he did not speak again until the usual age of speech.
rows.anchor: أيقنوا ببراءة أمه وأنها من أهل العصمة والبعد من الريبة

rows.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
rows.claim: An objection reads the resurrection phrase as proof that there is no life in the grave; the answer is that it means everlasting resurrection life, unlike the grave’s life.
rows.anchor: يدل على أن لا حياة في القبر لأنه ذكر حياة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barzakh life is intermediate: it is life of the spirit alone, while resurrection life joins spirit and body; spirits do not cease living after their creation.
rows.anchor: حياة البرزخ على النصف من حياة يوم البعث فإن الأولى حياة الروح فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: John’s peace is indefinite and Jesus’ definite because a little from God is much; Hasan’s reading of guide us to a straight path signals contentment with little.
rows.anchor: ثم إنه نكر في سلام يحيى وعرف في سلام عيسى لأن الأول من الله

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The sheikh explains that John’s third-person wording differs from Jesus’ first-person wording and says both possess the realities of annihilation and completeness.
rows.anchor: قال شيخي وسندي في "كتاب البرقيات" له قدس سره إنما أتى بطريق الغيبة

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report says John warned Jesus against feeling secure from God’s plan, while Jesus warned John against despairing of mercy; God loves the one with the better expectation of Him.
rows.anchor: أوحى الله تعالى إليهما أن أحبكما إلي أحسنكما ظنا بي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: John’s blood continued boiling until seventy thousand were killed in retaliation, while Jesus was raised to the highest heaven, manifesting beauty; each attained perfection in his station.
rows.anchor: فلم يزل فائرا دمه حتى قتل من أجله سبعون ألفا قصاصا منه

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Inwardly Jesus represents meaning born from divine breath in the heart, which can die under overpowering ego traits and practices; even the spiritually alive should not presume immunity.
rows.anchor: في "التأويلات النجمية" قوله : {ويوم أموت} فيه إشارة إلى أن عيسى المعنى المتولد

rows.speaker: التكملة
rows.claim: The account dates Jesus’ birth to the Successor kings, says Mary was thirteen, Jesus received prophethood at thirty and was raised at thirty-three, and Mary lived six years afterward.
rows.anchor: وكان حمل مريم به وهي ابنة ثلاث عشرة سنة ونبىء عيسى وهو ابن ثلاثين سنة

rows.speaker: التكملة
rows.claim: Mary took the young Jesus to Egypt with Joseph the carpenter to escape Herod; Persian envoys arrived because of a star and were warned by an angel not to tell Herod.
rows.anchor: وأمر الله مريم أن ينتقل به إلى مصر ومعهما يوسف بن يعقوب النجار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Jesus son of Mary refutes Christian descriptions by presenting him with their opposites and gives a forceful proof against them.
rows.anchor: لا ما يصفه النصارى وهو تكذيب لهم فيما يصفونه على الوجه الأبلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qawl al-haqq means the true statement; it is an accusative verbal emphasis, while This is Jesus son of Mary is parenthetical, and the doubters claim he is God’s son.
rows.anchor: قول الثابت والصدق وهو بالنصب على أنه مصدر مؤكد

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: A child is a part of its parent, so denying God a child denies division or composition; the source illustrates this with the Prophet’s statement that Fatima is a piece of him.
rows.anchor: فإن الولد جزؤ الوالد كما قال عليه السلام : "فاطمة بضعة مني"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is exalted above the Christians’ falsehood because the Eternal has no kind or genus.
rows.anchor: تنزيها عن بهتان النصارى لأنه ليس للقديم جنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God decrees an affair, He wills it to exist; His saying Be is a figurative description of immediate creation, without resistance or delay.
rows.anchor: القول ههنا مجاز عن سرعة الإيجاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus’ declaration that God is his Lord and theirs continues his statement I am God’s servant; worshiping God alone is the straight path from which no traveler strays.
rows.anchor: من تمام كلام عيسى عطف على قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Christian parties split: Nestorians called Jesus God’s son, Jacobites said God descended to earth and ascended, and Melkites called him God’s servant and prophet.
rows.anchor: فقالت النسطورية : هو ابن الله واليعقوبية هو الله هبط إلى الأرض

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: One inward group, the saints and truthful ones, worships through the law and spiritual path, traversing stations toward nearness to God.
rows.anchor: فرقة يعبدون الله بالسير على قدمي الشريعة والطريقة بالعبور على المقامات

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: A second inward group consists of ordinary believers who worship God through the outward law and its practices and are people of Paradise.
rows.anchor: فرقة يعبدون الله على صورة الشريعة وأعمالها وهم المؤمنون المسلمون

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: A third group follows desire and nature while claiming to worship God, like idolaters who claim their idols bring them near; these innovators, hypocrites, and people of ostentation face Hell.
rows.anchor: فرقة يعبدون الهوى على وفق الطبيعة ويزعمون أنهم يعبدون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers are the disputing groups; wayl is a fixed, enduring declaration of ruin, construed as a nominative subject rather than the original verbal curse.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على معنى ثبات الهلاك ودوامه للمدعو عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scene of the great day means witnessing the Resurrection with its terror, reckoning, and recompense.
rows.anchor: من شهود يوم عظيم الهول والحساب والجزاء وهو يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording marvels at how sharp the wrongdoers’ hearing and sight will be on the day they come for judgment, after they were deaf and blind to guidance in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وهو تعجب من حدة سمعهم وأبصارهم يومئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers are now in manifest error because they wholly neglected hearing and seeing when those faculties could benefit them.
rows.anchor: حيث أغفلوا الاستماع والنظر بالكلية حين ينفعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian admonition urges people not to waste precious time, since tomorrow they will regret failing to heed the truth.
rows.anchor: كه فرصت عزيزست والوقت سيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is told to warn the wrongdoers of the Day of Regret, when everyone grieves: sinners for their sins and the righteous for doing too little good.
rows.anchor: أما المسيىء فعلى إساءته وأما المحسن فعلى قلة إحسانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The affair is settled when reckoning ends and the two parties depart for Paradise or Hell.
rows.anchor: فرغ من الحساب وتصادر الفريقان إلى الجنة والنار

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Asked about that day, the Prophet said death will appear as a speckled white ram and be slaughtered; a caller announces everlasting life, deepening Paradise’s joy and Hell’s grief.
rows.anchor: حين يجاء بالموت على صورة الكبش الأملح فيذبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clauses about heedlessness and disbelief are circumstantial descriptions of those settled in manifest error.
rows.anchor: وهما جملتان حاليتان من الضمير المستتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone inherits the earth and everyone on it, leaving no one else any independent kingship or ownership; the subject was discussed earlier in Surat al-Hijr.
rows.anchor: لا يبقى لأحد غيرنا عليهم ملك ولا ملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All return to God for requital, with no other having an independent or shared claim over them.
rows.anchor: يردون للجزاء لا إلى غيرنا استقلالا واشتراكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There are two returns: ordinary people are compelled from souls attached to worldly life, while the elect return gently because they are detached from this world and the next and long for God and meeting Him.
rows.anchor: رجوع بالقهر وهو رجوع العوام لأن نفوسهم باقية مطمئنة بالدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A spiritual traveler should seek annihilation and abiding in God and deepen longing to meet Him, returning voluntarily before the compelled return.
rows.anchor: فعلى السالك أن يجتهد في تحصيل الفناء والبقاء وتكميل الشوق إلى اللقاء

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن المزين
rows.claim: Abu al-Hasan al-Muzayyin thought he was most self-denying until an unseen speaker rebuked his vanity; asceticism has degrees, so none should boast.
rows.anchor: يا حجام كم تحدث نفسك بالأباطيل فظهر أن الترك والتجرد والرجوع في الحق على مراتب

rows.speaker: إبراهيم الخواص
rows.claim: Ibrahim al-Khawwas endured hardship in the desert, then felt pride at Mecca; an old woman exposed his conceit and showed that success in returning to God is divine.
rows.anchor: فظهر أن التوفيق للرجوع إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The success of returning to God is from Him, and every perfection comes through His power, strength, support, and help.
rows.anchor: إنما هو من الله وكل كمال فبحوله وقوته ونصرته ومعونته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is told to recite Abraham’s story to his people: scriptural communities acknowledged Abraham and Arabs boasted descent from him, so his monotheism should move them away from idolatry.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن أهل الملل كانوا يعترفون بفضله ومشركو العرب يفتخرون بكونهم من أبنائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Siddiq means one who consistently and thoroughly tells the truth in all that he does.
rows.anchor: ملازما للصدق في كل ما يأتي وما يذر مبالغا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophethood entails truthfulness, but not every truthful saint is a prophet; spiritual truthfulness means effacement of self and abiding through God.
rows.anchor: ليس من شرط الصديق أن يكون نبيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ranks are sadiq, saddiq, and siddiq; a truthful person stands with, by, and in God, effaced from self and abiding through the Lord.
rows.anchor: ولأرباب الصدق مراتب صادق وصدوق وصديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A messenger is sent to convey rulings and may be an angel or human, whereas a prophet is specifically human.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين الرسول والنبي أن الرسول من بعث لتبليغ الأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time phrase is an inclusion replacing Abraham’s name, and the address to his father Azar begins gently and makes the appeal easy to accept.
rows.anchor: بدل من إبراهيم بدل الاشتمال لأن الأحيان مشتملة على ما فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In yā abati, tā substitutes for the possessive yāʾ, so it is not combined with it or a following alif.
rows.anchor: فإن التاء عوض عن ياء الإضافة ولذلك لا يجتمعان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idols cannot hear worshippers’ praise or see their submission, benefit them, or avert harm; mā refers to images and statues.
rows.anchor: وما عبارة عن الصور والتماثيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham says revelation has brought knowledge his father lacks and gently asks him to follow; he presents himself as a familiar guide rather than stressing his father’s ignorance or his own superiority.
rows.anchor: لم يشافهه بالجهل المفرط وإن كان في أقصاه ولم يصف نفسه بالعلم الفائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshipping idols is serving Satan because Satan decorates and incites it; his refusal to prostrate was rebellion against the Merciful, and obeying a rebel brings punishment.
rows.anchor: فإن عبادتك للأصنام عبادة له إذ هو الذي يزينها لك ويغريك عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham fears that dying in obedience to Satan will expose his father to punishment from the Merciful; the word fear softens the appeal, and Satan’s ally is close to him in the curse.
rows.anchor: إن مت على ما أنت عليه من متابعة الشيطان وعصيان الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The father answers stubbornly; the fronted question expresses astonishment that Abraham would turn from the idols, as though such rejection were irrational.
rows.anchor: أمعرض ومنصرف أنت عنها بتوجيه الإنكار إلى نفس الرغبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat is to stone Abraham to death or drive him away; another view takes stoning figuratively as verbal abuse and cursing.
rows.anchor: يعني : الشتم والذم ومنه الرجيم المرمي باللعن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to leave means keep away for a long time, remain safe from the father, and stop speaking to him.
rows.anchor: زمانا طويلا سالما مني ولا تكلمني من الملاوة وهو الدهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: R-j-m originally means throwing stones, from rijām, stones used for pelting.
rows.anchor: أصل الرجم الرمي بالرجام بالكسر وهي الحجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s peace is a farewell, not a prayer for kindness; it means he will not harm or insult his father, matching evil with good and permitting departure from an intractable person he advised.
rows.anchor: فهو سلام مفارقة لا سلام لطف وإحسان لأنه ليس بدعاء له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future either marks what comes next or adds emphasis; Abraham asks God to enable his father’s repentance and faith.
rows.anchor: بأن يوفقك للتوبة ويهديك إلى الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking a disbeliever’s guidance before despair of his faith is established is permissible; seeking forgiveness for one known to persist in disbelief or who dies that way is forbidden by revelation.
rows.anchor: الاستغفار بهذا المعنى للكافر قبل تبيين أنه يموت على الكفر مما لا ريب في جوازه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hafiy means exceedingly kind and generous in benevolence.
rows.anchor: حفيت به بالغت وتحفيت في إكرامه بالغت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham will emigrate away from his family and their idols because his advice failed, worship God alone, and humbly hopes not to be disappointed in prayer.
rows.anchor: أتباعد عنك وعن قومك بالمهاجرة بديني حيث لم يؤثر فيكم نصائحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beginning with perhaps shows humility and good manners.
rows.anchor: وفي تصدير الكلام بعسى إظهار التواضع ومراعاة حسن الأدب

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The sheikh says Abraham emigrated from Kutha to the Holy Land; God then gave him Isaac and Isaac’s son Jacob, not immediately upon departure, since the nearby promised child was Ishmael.
rows.anchor: قال في "تفسير الشيخ" : فارتحل من كوثي إلى الأرض المقدسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Isaac and Jacob are singled out as the prophetic lineage, or because Ishmael’s merit will be discussed separately; every one of them was made a prophet.
rows.anchor: ولعل تخصيصهما بالذكر لأنهما شجرة الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kullan is placed first as the direct object for emphasis: every one of them, not only some, was made a prophet.
rows.anchor: كل واحد منهم جعلناه نبيا لا بعضهم دون بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God granted Abraham’s family every kind of religious and worldly good beyond what is given to others.
rows.anchor: كل خير ديني ودنيوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A high good reputation means lofty praise; tongue stands for speech or the Arab tongue, and people take pride in and praise the family, fulfilling Abraham’s prayer.
rows.anchor: فإن لسان الصدق هو الثناء الحسن على أن يكون المراد باللسان ما يوجد به من الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage teaches gentleness and good character: a guide should be gentle because harshness drives listeners away; good character even toward unbelievers earns divine shelter and nearness.
rows.anchor: فإن العنف يوجب إعراض المستمع

rows.speaker: الصائب
rows.claim: The poet says that speaking harshly in the past has brought the addressee only the grinding mill of teeth.
rows.anchor: قال الصائب : كذشت عمرو نكردى كلام خودرا نرم

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم
rows.claim: The path to God is following: higher ranks follow scripture, then the Messenger, then Companions, and lower ranks follow saints and scholars of God.
rows.anchor: عليه السلام ومن نزل عنهم اتبع الصحابة رضي الله عنهم ومن نزل عنهم

rows.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Sahl ibn Abd Allah says imitation is especially hard on the ego because it offers neither breath nor ease.
rows.anchor: لأن سهل بن عبد الله قال : أشد ما على النفس الاقتداء فإنه ليس للنفس فيه نفس

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم
rows.claim: To be safe inwardly and outwardly in this life and the next, one should leave bad companions and pray for God to enable the separation, since a person is with whom they love.
rows.anchor: ومنها العزلة قال أبو القاسم : من أراد السلامة في الدنيا والآخرة ظاهرا وباطنا

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: Seclusion quiets the tongue and has two forms: seekers withdraw bodily from others, while realized knowers withdraw their hearts from creation into divine witnessing.
rows.anchor: وهي على قسمين : عزلة المريدين بالأجسام عن الأغيار وعزلة المحققين بالقلوب عن الأكوان

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: Seclusion may avoid people’s harm or one’s own, the latter higher because self-suspicion is better; the highest prefers God’s company, whose gifts are unknown to outsiders.
rows.anchor: وإما اتقاء شره المتعدي إليهم وهو أرفع من الأول إذ سوء الظن بالنفس أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seclusion quiets the tongue but not necessarily the heart, which can dwell on what is not God; silence is a separate pillar of the path, and emigration from evildoers brings divine honor.
rows.anchor: العزلة تعطي صمت اللسان لا صمت القلب
